findings.title: Deadline recovery can return ROLLED_BACK while a forward mutation is still running
findings.observation: The deadline races each oracle against a timer, aborts its signal, then rejects after a five-second grace period regardless of whether the oracle stopped. Recovery immediately persists and returns the rollback suffix. Active host operations pass the signal only into pg_dump/age and age/pg_restore; their Docker Compose, inspect and scenario-runner work does not accept it. Those promises therefore continue after Promise.race settles.
findings.trigger: Start a forward host operation shortly before the four-hour boundary so a Docker Compose or other signal-ignoring call is still pending when the controller hard stop fires.
findings.impact: The attempt can report ROLLED_BACK and release its lock, then the old forward operation can create or replace resources afterward. That breaks the journal's terminal invariant, can race a new authorized attempt and can re-enable or recreate state that rollback just removed.

evidence.description: Exact-head synthetic oracle ignored AbortSignal. runDeployment returned ROLLED_BACK with one rollback while the forward mutation flag was false, then the same oracle set it true after the terminal return.
The hard-stop Promise rejects after the grace period without joining the oracle promise.
The host RunDocker contract has no AbortSignal; default execFile timeout is independent and 28 host calls use it, including restore Compose creation and mutation.
The committed hung-phase test cooperatively rejects on abort, so it cannot detect an ignored signal or a late side effect.

findings.remediation: Fence every active mutation with cancellation that reaches the underlying process/request and do not begin or return terminal recovery until the in-flight forward operation is definitively stopped or reconciled. Pass the attempt signal/deadline through RunDocker and other mutation adapters, await process termination, and preserve exactly-once rollback ordering.
findings.verification: Add a deliberately non-cooperative/delayed host operation at every mutating phase. The controller must never return a terminal state or release authority while it can still mutate; after rollback and after an additional delay, side-effect count and resource state must remain unchanged.

findings.title: Restore cleanup can be recorded before an in-flight Compose operation creates resources
findings.observation: The new lifecycle correctly removes resources that are present and quiescent, but RESTORE_ENVIRONMENT's compose up ignores the controller signal. On deadline, rollback cleanup can observe an empty project, persist CLEANED, and return before that older compose up finishes and creates the container/volume. The lifecycle then suppresses future cleanup unless it notices resources have reappeared, while the current invocation has already ended.
findings.trigger: Let restore Compose creation remain pending across the attempt deadline, with its resources appearing only after cleanup's observation and terminal return.
findings.impact: The exact isolated database/app/volume may survive a failed attempt despite a durable CLEANED claim, retaining restored data and blocking deterministic reuse. This is the explicit failure/crash case PRR-006 required to close.

evidence.description: Restore intent precedes compose up, but the compose call cannot consume context.signal.
Cleanup observes once, optionally runs compose down, re-observes, and persists CLEANED; it has no fence against the still-running creator.
Lifecycle tests use static resource lists, and the deadline test uses a cooperative abstract oracle; neither schedules resource creation after CLEANED.
The approved design requires deadline abort and stale recovery to verify zero resources remain and persist cleanup before terminalization.

findings.remediation: Make restore creation and every later restore mutation terminate or join before cleanup observes the project. Bind cleanup to a quiescent creator generation/lease, then prove no matching resources can appear after CLEANED; keep backup and production outside cleanup authority.
findings.verification: Delay resource creation until after abort and inject faults before/during/after compose up, migration, app start and scenario replay. Each case must await all creators, leave zero exact resources after a post-terminal delay, preserve backup bytes/production identity and record cleanup only after quiescence.
